summary: S. 4392, the Energy Security Pacts Act, authorizes the Secretary of State to establish multiyear agreements called Energy Security Pacts with eligible partner countries. The goal is to enhance energy and mineral security, promote reliable access to energy or electricity, and diversify supply chains. The bill creates an Office of Energy Security Pacts, a Director position, and an interagency Energy Security Pacts Council to coordinate activities, negotiate pacts, and oversee projects.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible nations may enter into multiyear agreements with the United States to receive technical support, grants, and administrative capacity-building for energy and mineral security projects.
The Department of State and member agencies of the Energy Security Pacts Council will coordinate, detail staff, and execute interagency agreements to support pact implementation.

Projects must undergo assessments regarding potential impacts on domestic supplier competitiveness and production displacement, and pacts aim to support the commercial competitiveness of U.S. companies.

key_provisions: Authorizes the Secretary of State to establish multiyear Energy Security Pacts with eligible partner countries to enhance energy and economic security and diversify critical mineral and energy supply chains.
Establishes an Office of Energy Security Pacts led by a Director appointed by the Secretary to manage pact development, negotiation, and implementation.
Establishes an Energy Security Pacts Council chaired by the Secretary and composed of officials from various executive departments and agencies to coordinate activities and make recommendations.
Sets specific eligibility requirements for partner countries based on income levels, presence of critical minerals or adversary threats, and exclusion of covered nations.

Prohibits military assistance or training, projects that cause significant environmental or safety hazards, and financial assistance to entities tied to senior U.S. government officials or their immediate families.
Requires the Comptroller General of the United States to submit an annual evaluation of the efficiency and development impact of supported projects to Congress starting two years after enactment.

summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a structured interagency framework and diplomatic instrument to coordinate U.S. foreign assistance and infrastructure investments related to foreign energy and critical mineral sectors over a 15-year period for new pacts.
